domain: application shell frontend migration / CI governance / generated-artifact controls

scope.summary: Remove the retired SolidJS/SolidStart app-shell skeleton and shrink active CI, catalog, manifest, gate policy, current planning references, and live client-stack discovery so Leptos remains the only active app-shell/frontend target.
explicit_non_claims: This change does not implement a new Leptos UI feature, route, tenant workflow, or production runtime behavior.
Historical ADR, audit, and evidence records that mention SolidJS are retained as provenance; active source/config references are removed or converted into fail-closed denylist tests.
No generated JSON face is hand-edited; generated architecture/index mirrors remain source-generated surfaces and are not manually rewritten in this slice.
No new dependency, package manager, Node build path, or provider SDK is introduced.
No Codex/OMX ultragoal completion is claimed by this slice; it is one verified migration cleanup in the broader hyperscaler reorg.

comparable_surfaces: AWS/GCP-scale CI fan-in hygiene: retired build lanes must not remain required contexts.
Google-style monorepo cleanup: deleted product skeletons must be removed from active registries, generated-artifact policies, and lint baselines in the same change.
Enterprise frontend platform governance: superseded stacks remain in historical ADRs but cannot reappear in active manifests.
hyperscaler_lens.improved_criterion: retired-stack removal, CI fan-in hygiene, and active manifest discipline
hyperscaler_lens.provider_neutrality: The slice removes a Node/SolidJS/pnpm surface and adds no cloud-provider, package-manager, or third-party SDK coupling.
hyperscaler_lens.merge_conflict_resistance: The only large deletion is a retired tree; active edits are narrow governance/control-plane files plus a unique append-only evidence JSON.

facets.F1_correctness: The tracked SolidJS app-shell tree is deleted; active references in CI fan-in, current planning docs, capability registry, design deferred surfaces, generated-artifact gate fixtures, rust-first policy, maturity claims, and client manifests are updated; the live client-stack gate now scans the active crate-shaped app-shell manifest.
facets.F2_tests: Targeted Buck2 tests/builds, the new client-stack CLI regression target, live client-stack gate, JSON/YAML parsing, residual searches, and git diff whitespace checks verify the cleanup without using Cargo as final authority.
facets.F3_maintainability: Removing the retired frontend tree and app-shell-codegen lane eliminates a parallel Node/SolidJS maintenance path while tightening a single Rust lint against reintroduction.
facets.F4_compatibility: Historical ADR/audit/evidence references are preserved; current planning docs now name the Leptos shell, while active Leptos manifest authority is unchanged except for removing a retired fallback label.
facets.F5_security: The diff deletes package manager/dependency surfaces, removes active banned-framework fallback text from the app-shell manifest, and introduces no secrets, unsafe Rust, shell expansion, network path, auth logic, or data-handling behavior.
facets.F6_privacy: No tenant data, user content, PII, telemetry payload, or persistence path is added or changed.
facets.F7_operability: The single required CI fan-in no longer waits on the removed app-shell codegen lane, and rust-first hygiene accounting now reflects the smaller workflow surface.
facets.F8_performance: CI avoids a retired pnpm install/codegen/typecheck job; no runtime hot path is added.
facets.F9_compliance: No *.generated.json files are hand-edited; evidence is recorded under evidence/multispectrum; generated mirrors are left to their producer pipeline.
facets.F10_reversibility: Rollback is a normal git revert restoring the deleted tree, CI job, and policy rows; no data migration or production state mutation occurs.
facets.F11_observability: No runtime instrumentation is changed; the residue class is observable through the live client-stack gate now reporting at least one checked manifest and through recorded verification evidence.
facets.F13_migration: Completes the active-code/current-planning portion of the ADR-0393 SolidJS-to-Leptos retirement by removing the old skeleton and active build/governance references.
facets.M1_challenge_assumption: Did not erase historical ADR/audit/evidence mentions because they are governance provenance; instead, active manifests and source/config are purged and linted fail-closed.
facets.M2_zoomed_out_fit: This is a narrow prerequisite cleanup for the hyperscaler reorg: it removes a conflicting frontend substrate so future product lanes build on the canonical Rust/Leptos foundation.

fixed_findings: Tightened the client-stack lint so even retired/forbidden SolidJS wording fails in active manifests.
Removed app-shell-codegen from both the workflow fan-in and rust-first inline-shell baseline instead of only deleting files.
Replaced generated-artifact gate fixture references to retired app-shell generated paths with neutral legacy/generated fixture names.
Reviewer fix-loop: expanded live client-manifest discovery beyond clients/<surface>/client-manifest.json, added crate-shaped CLI regressions, and confirmed the repo gate checks 1 active manifest.
residual_gaps: Remote oya-ci-required is pending until branch push and protected PR execution.
Full product/UI maturity remains outside this cleanup slice.
pre_pr_review.torvald_lens: Deleting a dead tree is good; pretending this makes the UI mature would be garbage. The honest claim is residue removal plus gates that stop it coming back.
